extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers using structural equation modeling (SEM) in social sciences, particularly journalism/media studies
extracted.subtask_short: SEM model testing for journalism study
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and revising a structural equation model of reporters' perceptions of influences on media content: includes measurement-model (CFA) evaluation, structural-path assessment, modification steps, cross-validation, and follow-up correlational and regression analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-step modeling approach (measurement then structural)
rubrics_metrics.description: The two-step modeling approach reserves the first stage for examining the measurement portion of the model (i.e., CFAs for unobserved constructs with their respective indicators) before evaluating the structural portion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include structural-only variables (e.g., Market Size) in the measurement-model stage; evaluate and validate the measurement model (CFAs) first, then move to testing structural paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model fit indices to report
rubrics_metrics.description: Report multiple fit indices: chi-square (χ2) and degrees of freedom, CFI, TLI, SRMR, RMSEA (with p-close) and the 90% confidence interval for RMSEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a full set of indices (e.g., χ2 (47) = 133.082, CFI = .96, TLI = .94, SRMR = .0575, RMSEA = .077, p-close = .002, 90% CI .062–.093) because any single index can be misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting chi-square and sensitivity to sample size
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the chi-squared test statistic may be significant, other fit indices should be considered when assessing overall model fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize chi-square's sensitivity to sample size (large samples often yield significant χ2); use alternative fit indices (CFI/TLI/RMSEA/SRMR) to judge practical fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: RMSEA and p-close interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use RMSEA as an index of approximate fit and interpret p-close and the RMSEA confidence interval against recommended cutoffs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply rules of thumb (e.g., Kline): consider lower bound ≤ .05 and upper bound ≤ .10 for the 90% CI; a significant p-close or lower bound above .05 sends a mixed or poor-fit message even if point RMSEA is acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple indices rather than single-rule cutoff
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate model fit holistically using several indices rather than relying on a single statistic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When some indices conflict (e.g., significant χ2 but acceptable CFI/TLI/SRMR/RMSEA), report all and justify model acceptability based on the pattern and theoretical considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model modification procedure: examine output and theoretical justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify the model based on empirical output (e.g., nonsignificant paths, modification indices) only when changes are theoretically sensible and face-valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make changes one at a time and assess output after each change. Provide theoretical rationale for each modification (e.g., moving Market Size to affect Extramedia Influences because it is plausible reporters in larger markets report fewer extramedia pressures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling nonsignificant paths: consider mediation/relocation rather than deletion
rubrics_metrics.description: When a structural path is nonsignificant (e.g., Market Size → Content Influence/Outcome), consider alternative specifications such as indirect effects or moving the variable to predict a different construct rather than removing it outright.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from study: instead of removing Market Size, hypothesize Market Size → Extramedia Influences (an indirect effect on content) because it was theoretically plausible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deciding between covariance and direct paths
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose whether to model two constructs as covarying or as having a direct causal path based on whether a construct is exogenous/endogenous and theoretical expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a previously exogenous construct becomes endogenous after moving variables (e.g., Extramedia Influences), change covariance to a direct path when theory supports a directional effect (e.g., Extramedia → Organizational Influences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Report standardized regression weights and variance explained (R2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report standardized regression weights for paths and the percentage of variance in dependent constructs explained by the model (e.g., model accounted for 92% of variance in Content Influence/Outcome in exploratory sample; 90% in full sample).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide these values to indicate effect magnitudes and model explanatory power; include tables/figures of paths with standardized coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-validation: confirmatory testing on withheld and full samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-evaluate the revised model using a withheld (confirmatory) subfile and the full sample to confirm findings and generalizability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report fit indices for each test (exploratory, confirmatory, full sample) and show consistency or explain discrepancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of multivariate normality and use of bootstrapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Check multivariate normality (e.g., Mardia’s coefficient); if non-normality is present or borderline (e.g., Mardia’s kurtosis = 6.077), compare Maximum Likelihood estimates with bootstrapped estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run bootstrapping (e.g., 2,000 samples with replacement) and compare estimates and standard errors; if no sizeable differences, reporting ML estimates is acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decompose and report direct, indirect, and total effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate and present direct, indirect (mediated) and total effects among latent constructs, and explain how indirect effects are calculated (product of component direct effects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a table of standardized direct, indirect, and total effects and illustrate interpretation (e.g., Organizational → Within-Media = .679 and Within-Media → Content = .587, so indirect = .679 × .587 = .399; total = direct + indirect).

rubrics_metrics.name: Variable coding and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Document how key variables are measured and coded (e.g., Market Size measured by DMAs and reverse-coded so larger numbers correspond to larger media markets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state coding choices and rationale to avoid confusion for researcher and reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use partial correlations to control for confounds
rubrics_metrics.description: When assessing bivariate relationships that may be influenced by a third variable (e.g., Market Size), use partial correlations to hold that variable constant and compare with zero-order correlations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret changes in coefficients to determine whether the control variable affects the strength or significance of relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report effect sizes and caution about sample-size-driven significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Alongside p-values, report and interpret effect sizes (e.g., correlation r, percent variance explained) and acknowledge when significant results have small effect sizes that may be due to large sample size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note small effect sizes (e.g., r ≈ .15 accounts for ~3% variance) and caution when generalizing findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of commonality analysis to partition explained variance
rubrics_metrics.description: Use commonality analysis to describe unique and shared contributions of predictors to R2 and identify the strongest predictors (e.g., Advertiser Pressures uniquely explains ~11% of variance in content influence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report unique contributions, shared contributions between predictors, and totals to understand predictor interrelationships and parsimony trade-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regression reporting conventions and diagnostics
rubrics_metrics.description: When conducting multiple regression, report model statistics (F, R2/adjusted R2), unstandardized coefficients (B), standard errors (SE B), standardized beta (β), t-statistics, and p-values; inspect for suppression or multicollinearity effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret unexpected beta signs as possible suppressor variables and discuss (e.g., Staff Size Pressure had positive correlation but negative standardized beta, suggesting suppression).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include correlated measurement errors and covariances when justified
rubrics_metrics.description: Report covariances/correlated measurement errors among measured indicators when they are present and justified (e.g., e5 ↔ e4; e2 ↔ e3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document these correlations in tables and provide theoretical or measurement-based rationales for allowing correlated errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence empirical modifications and document decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Make and document model changes sequentially (one at a time), assess output after each, and record justification for each modification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example statement used: 'Each change was made one at a time and the output was assessed before making subsequent changes.' Use this disciplined sequence to avoid data-driven overfitting.
